reproductions.title: KISS-ICP: In Defense of Point-to-Point ICP — Simple, Accurate, and Robust Registration If Done the Right Way
reproductions.static_status: 🟡 **代码跑通并出数**（0.409 %）；⚠️ **数字与论文不可直接比**，原因见下
reproductions.heading: 01-02 · KISS-ICP

checks.name: official_pipeline_reports_all_metrics
checks.detail: ATE 0.112 m, avg translation 0.409 %, avg rotation 0.005 deg/m, 50.0 Hz, 20.0 ms/frame

checks.name: every_frame_processed
checks.detail: 141 poses written for 141 input scans

checks.name: trajectory_matches_the_source_data
checks.detail: ground-truth path length 108.3 m against the 108.3 m measured on the benchmark release - a mismatch would mean the pose inversion in make_kitti_seq.py is wrong

findings.name: cannot_reproduce_the_published_number_on_free_data
findings.detail: KISS-ICP's metric is the KITTI devkit one: segments of {100..800} m starting every 10 frames. This trajectory is 108.3 m, so it yields exactly 2 error sample(s). The paper's 0.5 % averages hundreds of samples over the full KITTI sequences (thousands of metres each). 2 samples is a sanity run, not a reproduction.

findings.name: all_four_paper_datasets_are_gated
findings.detail: KITTI odometry needs registration (~80 GB), MulRan needs registration, Boreas needs a form, and Newer College's download page carries no direct links (its download is reported broken upstream). Reproducing the published numbers requires registering for KITTI.

findings.name: kiss_icp_1_3_0_breaks_on_numpy_2
findings.detail: pipeline.py:130 calls float() on a shape-(1,) timestamp array, which NumPy 2 no longer allows. The crash is in the TUM-format writer, which runs after _run_evaluation() - so no metric is affected, but without the one-line patch in work/local_patches.patch the run dies before returning them.

findings.name: no_loop_closure_by_design
findings.detail: there is no loop closure, no pose graph and no keyframe selection - 141 frames, 50 Hz, 20 ms/frame on CPU. Drift is bounded only by ICP itself, which matters for the H1' experiment in 01-01: a 'cleaned map hurts localization' result could be drift rather than map quality.

reproductions.note: KISS-ICP on a reconstructed 141-frame KITTI 00 sub-sequence: ATE 0.112 m, avg translation error 0.409 % over only 2 metric sample(s) - the paper's 0.5 % is NOT reproduced (see findings)

checks.name: published_output_reproduces_paper_table_ii
checks.detail: the authors' own estimate/00_ERASOR.pcd scored with their own analysis_runner against their own GT gives 93.979/97.081/0.9550 against Table II's 93.98/97.081/0.955 - so the evaluator, the GT and the voxel rule are the paper's

checks.name: official_pipeline_runs_on_official_data
checks.detail: mapgen + offline_map_updater over the official bag produced 374393 points (the authors' published estimate/00_ERASOR.pcd holds 364005)

checks.name: our_run_lands_in_the_upstream_band
checks.detail: PR 95.622 / RR 94.412 / F1 0.9501; the paper's Table II is 93.98/97.081/0.955 and the authors' re-run on current master is 95.79/95.642/0.957

checks.name: benchmark_port_still_reproduces_its_row
checks.detail: benchmark port SA/DA/AA = 66.71/98.54/81.07 vs Table I 66.7/98.54/81.07

findings.name: official_and_port_agree_on_erasor_where_removert_disagreed
findings.detail: ERASOR's official repo scores PR 95.62 / RR 94.41 / F1 0.9501 on the official snippet, and the benchmark's ROS-free port reproduces its own Table I row (SA/DA/AA = 66.71/98.54/81.07) on the Zenodo sequence. Unlike Removert (01-04, where the port lost 47.7 pp of dynamic rejection), here the two implementations do not contradict each other - the metric changes, the method does not.

findings.name: the_27_point_gap_is_the_metric_not_the_method
findings.detail: on the same sequence, the same method reads PR 95.62 under the paper's voxel-wise metric and SA 66.71 under the benchmark's point-wise one. The paper's own number is the higher one, and the benchmark's GT cloud has 17362230 points against our map's 374393 - at 0.05 m nearest-neighbour, resolution loss is scored as deletion.

reproductions.note: official ERASOR on the authors' seq-00 snippet: PR/RR/F1 = 95.62/94.41/0.950 (paper Table II 93.98/97.081/0.955)

reproductions.title: Removert: Remove then Revert — Static Map Building in Challenging Environment
reproductions.heading: 01-04 · Removert

checks.name: official_pipeline_produced_a_static_map
checks.detail: results/removert_kitti00/map_static/StaticMapScansideMapGlobal.pcd holds 4628181 points after mapgen+removert ran over all 141 frames

checks.name: evaluator_implementations_agree
checks.detail: official export_eval_pcd vs scipy re-implementation: 0 disagreeing GT labels (rate 0.0)

findings.name: official_removert_is_not_the_conservative_extreme
findings.detail: same 141 frames, same evaluator, same GT: official Removert scores SA 99.62 / DA 89.25 / AA 94.29, the benchmark's port scores SA 99.44 / DA 41.53 / AA 64.26. Static preservation is unchanged (0.2 pp apart) but dynamic rejection differs by 47.7 pp - the port leaks more than half the dynamic points the official code removes. Any ranking built on the port under-rates Removert.

findings.name: removert_revert_step_matters_more_than_it_looks
findings.detail: map-side output at the finest removal resolution scores SA 95.15 / DA 98.97 (AA 97.04) against the scan-side merged output's SA 99.62 / DA 89.25 (AA 94.29). The two upstream outputs of one run sit at opposite corners of the precision/recall trade-off, so 'Removert's score' is not defined without saying which output is submitted.

findings.name: official_output_is_downsampled_but_still_scores_higher
findings.detail: the official map has 4628181 points against the port's 16722918. The evaluator's 0.05 m nearest-neighbour rule punishes sparse maps, so the official run wins on DA despite submitting a map ~3.6x smaller - the extra points in the port are not in the places the metric looks at.

reproductions.note: official Removert (irapkaist/removert) on KITTI 00: SA/DA/AA = 99.62/89.25/94.29; benchmark port 99.44/41.53/64.26

reproductions.title: DUFOMap: Efficient Dynamic Awareness Mapping
reproductions.static_status: 🟢 **已复现：与论文 2 位小数完全一致**
reproductions.heading: 01-05 · DUFOMap

checks.name: reproduces_paper_headline
checks.detail: d_p=1 gives SA/DA/AA = 97.96/98.72/98.34 vs paper 97.96/98.72/98.34 (Table I p.5), within 0.5 pp

checks.name: gt_is_binary_and_rare_dynamic
checks.detail: GT = 17266247 static + 95983 dynamic points (0.55% dynamic) - a rare-positive problem, so AA is dominated by SA

checks.name: dp_is_load_bearing
checks.detail: d_p=2 keeps +1.92 pp more static and removes -2.09 pp fewer dynamic points than the paper's d_p=1

findings.name: upstream_example_contradicts_the_paper
findings.detail: DynamicMap_Benchmark's methods/dufomap/main.py passes d_p=2 with the comment 'same with paper', but the DUFOMap paper's default - the one whose Table I row we reproduce - is d_p=1 (Table IV, p.7). Using the example's value reproduces AA only by coincidence; SA and DA are each off by about 2 pp.

findings.name: geometric_mean_hides_the_sa_da_tradeoff
findings.detail: d_p=1 -> SA 97.96 / DA 98.72 / AA 98.34; d_p=2 -> SA 99.89 / DA 96.63 / AA 98.25. The two AA values are 0.09 pp apart while SA and DA each move ~2 pp in opposite directions - the geometric mean of a rare-positive problem is almost entirely SA, so it cannot tell a conservative cleaner from an aggressive one.

findings.name: dynamic_points_are_0_55_percent_of_the_map
findings.detail: 95983 of 17362230 GT points are dynamic; any metric averaged over points is therefore a static-preservation metric in disguise.

reproductions.note: DUFOMap on KITTI 00: SA/DA/AA = 97.96/98.72/98.34 vs paper 97.96/98.72/98.34

reproductions.title: BeautyMap: Binary-Encoded Adaptable Ground Matrix for Dynamic Points Removal in Global Maps
reproductions.heading: 01-06 · BeautyMap

checks.name: reproduces_paper_row
checks.detail: SA/DA/HA = 96.95/98.34/97.64 vs BeautyMap Table I p.6 96.76/98.38/97.56, within 0.5 pp

checks.name: aa_and_ha_agree_only_because_sa_da_are_close
checks.detail: AA 97.6431 vs HA 97.6407 - the two means differ by 0.0024 pp here because SA and DA are within 1.4 pp of each other. That is a property of this method on this sequence, not of the metrics.

findings.name: upstream_does_not_run_on_numpy_2
findings.detail: BeautyMap's vendored utils/pcdpy3.py calls np.fromstring (line 150) and ndarray.tostring (line 265), both removed in NumPy 2. Two LOCAL PATCHed lines (frombuffer(...).copy() and tobytes(order='C')) are required. The first failure is at read time; the second only after ~50 s of processing, at write time - a fresh clone that patches only the first looks fine until it has done all the work.

findings.name: matches_the_benchmark_papers_HA_column_too
findings.detail: This run also reproduces the HA column that the BeautyMap paper prints for the other methods: Removert 41.53/58.59 and ERASOR 98.54/79.55 predicted from this paper's Table I, and measured here as 41.5313/58.591 and 98.5352/79.5563. Two papers and four methods now agree on the same numbers, which is the strongest evidence we have that the whole data-and-evaluation chain is right.

findings.name: beautymap_is_the_balanced_one
findings.detail: BeautyMap SA 96.95 / DA 98.34 sits between Removert's refuse-to-delete (99.44/41.53) and ERASOR's delete-too-much (66.71/98.54), and is the only one of the four with both above 96.

reproductions.note: BeautyMap on KITTI 00: SA/DA/HA = 96.95/98.34/97.64 vs paper 96.76/98.38/97.56

reproductions.note: GPU/CUDA absent, and DynoSAM cannot even `cmake`-configure without it: dynosam_nn/CMakeLists.txt:3 declares `LANGUAGES C CXX CUDA`, :105 compiles a .cu source, :128-129 link TensorRT + cudart unconditionally, and FeatureTracker.hpp:33 includes <opencv2/cudaoptflow.hpp> with no guard (nvcc/NvInfer.h/CUDA OpenCV are all absent here). Runtime flags cannot help - the no-TensorRT path is already the default. Evidence: work/feasibility.md. Needs a CUDA GPU, not data or code changes.

reproductions.title: NGD-SLAM: Towards Real-Time Dynamic SLAM without GPU
reproductions.static_status: 🟢 **已复现：ATE 与 RPE-平移命中论文**；RPE-旋转有一处未解差异
reproductions.heading: 01-08 · NGD-SLAM

checks.name: reproduces_paper_ate
checks.detail: ATE (rigid, no scale) = 0.0157 m vs paper 0.015 m (Table I p.5, f3/walking_xyz), within 0.003

checks.name: reproduces_paper_rpe_translation
checks.detail: RPE translation = 0.0201 m/s vs paper 0.02 m/s, within 0.003

checks.name: every_frame_was_processed
checks.detail: 827 poses written; the paper requires processing all 827 frames, and both mechanisms (mask propagation and optical flow) depend on frame-to-frame continuity

findings.name: rotational_rpe_depends_on_an_unspecified_convention
findings.detail: our rotational RPE is 0.604 °/s by RMSE but 0.475 °/s by mean, against the paper's 0.47 °/s. The column is headed only 'RPE rotation (°/s)'. The distribution is skewed (median far below the max), which is exactly when the choice matters. Translation shows the same asymmetry but much smaller, so it happens to agree either way.

findings.name: cheap_semantics_is_the_actual_contribution
findings.detail: reading the official source, the system DOES use a neural network (YOLO-fastest-xl at 320x320, System.cc:217) - what it removes is the tracker's dependency on waiting for it (Tracking.cc:1592 never blocks, Tracking.cc:4286 propagates the old mask with LK optical flow). So it is a scheduling result, not a geometry-only result, and it inherits COCO's blind spot for unknown dynamic objects.

findings.name: wall_clock_is_the_same_order_as_the_paper
findings.detail: mean tracking 20.76 ms/frame vs the paper's 16.72 ms (~60 FPS). Measured headless on different hardware, so this supports 'same order of magnitude on CPU', not an exact match.

reproductions.note: NGD-SLAM on TUM fr3/walking_xyz: ATE 0.0157 m vs paper 0.015 m; RPE trans 0.0201 m/s vs 0.02
